done.why: I was two markers deep in a maze of twisty little passages, about to step west, when it told me I'd used all 30 turns. I'd have given the maze maybe five more moves before quitting anyway.

about: The old white-house-and-cellar adventure, but somebody's been renovating it: you grab the lamp and sword, go down the trap door, kill the troll, and then the way east is literally unfinished with a note from 'The Management', and the way west is a maze that loops you straight back to the troll room.

moments.note: Trap door slammed and barred behind me the moment I went down. Sword started glowing. Good hook.
Troll 'appears to have an axe to grind with you.' Made me laugh mid-fight.
East passage 'has not been finished. Back soon. -- The Management.' The game admitting it's under construction, in character.
Maze room described as just 'Maze' with nothing else. Started feeling the dread.
North then east from the maze put me back in the Troll Room. Didn't expect the maze to spit me out so fast.
My leaflet was sitting there when I went west from the Troll Room, so two different routes land in the same maze cell. Actually useful: the markers work.

wished: Read the note on the unfinished east passage more closely or do something with it; it felt like the most interesting thing down there and it was a dead end.
Have the maze rooms differ at all, even one word, so dropping junk isn't the only way to tell them apart.
Get the trap door back open, or at least know who barred it.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: First moment I felt the place had someone else in it.

lines.line: The troll, angered and humiliated, recovers his weapon. He appears to have an axe to grind with you.
lines.why: The fight was a slog of misses and this one line made it worth it.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: Funny, and it told me this isn't the version I half-remember, which is what kept me going into the maze.

lines.line:
Maze
A small leaflet is on the ground.
lines.why: Proof my marker trick worked and the maze is small and loopy, not endless.

fun.why: The opening and the troll fight moved fast and had jokes; the maze killed the momentum right as the turns ran out.

engagement.why: The barred door and the Management note made me curious enough to push into the maze, but the maze itself gave me nothing to be curious about.

difficulty.why: Nothing was hard; the troll took five swings but I never had to think. The maze was tedious rather than difficult.

interestingness.why: The changes from the classic (barred door, unfinished passage with a note, a maze right off the troll room) were the interesting parts; the rest was familiar furniture.

prose.why: Short, dry, and the fight messages have real character. The maze is the one place the prose goes flat on purpose.
